scope: Birmingham Terminal Station as it stood circa 1913, with its west-facing Byzantine Revival headhouse, paired towers, auxiliary wings, recessed subway approach and attached reinforced-concrete train shed.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Marye’s 1909 American Architect report and plates establish the 130-ft towers, 100-ft dome, buff-to-terracotta brick, terracotta roofs, grey sandstone, bronze frames, subway geometry, and reinforced concrete umbrella sheds. Qualla’s exact 1909–10 and 1913 exterior postcards establish facade details and massing.

The named station outline and shed on 1911 Sanborn sheet 21 establish each building mass. The trace is registered to the surviving Fifth Avenue North tunnel and Carraway corridor. The architect gives overall site and canopy dimensions.
